title: arXiv biology & biomedicine — daily report, 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from category listings and checkable paper/proceedings metadata, not measured readership or downloads. The arXiv corpus is incomplete for biomedical research, especially experimental and clinical preprints, and does not represent the biomedical literature as a whole.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Ten notable papers from today's configured biology and biomedicine categories show an emphasis on evaluating AI-assisted methods against explicit evidence: experimental follow-up, molecular dynamics, held-out genomic regions, and carefully specified imaging or simulation benchmarks. The lead stories concern drug discovery, single-cell gene regulation and protein design; the rest span docking, cancer prediction, channel kinetics and medical physics. This is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not an official popularity list, and arXiv covers only part of biomedical research, particularly omitting much experimental and clinical preprint activity.

sections.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
sections.abstract: The authors present an agent system and benchmark for end-to-end drug-discovery workflows, reporting three investigations whose findings received human-run experimental follow-up.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe Paper2Skill and parallel-agent exploration as supporting scientific decisions, with experimental follow-up for three discovery scenarios; this is a prototype, not a general demonstration of autonomous drug development.
sections.unique_caveat: The experimental demonstrations are three selected scenarios and were carried out by people; they do not establish prospective success rates, therapeutic efficacy, or clinical utility.

sections.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
sections.abstract: MUSS combines DNA-derived peak and gene representations with paired single-cell chromatin-accessibility and expression data to predict regulatory readouts, including for held-out genomic regions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report competitive expression prediction, enhancer–gene linking and cell-clustering results using a frozen sequence encoder plus multi-scale attention, including tests on unseen genes/peaks.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational evaluation, not experimental confirmation of regulatory causality. The authors note that enhancer–gene evaluation does not establish generalization to unseen links and that exact peak attention is costly.

sections.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a 220-case motif-scaffolding benchmark and an all-atom dynamics evaluation, finding that static refolding success often does not imply dynamic fidelity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that target coverage, unique-solution yield and MD-supported dynamical fidelity should be reported separately; only 8 of 55 evaluated pairs passed all their checks.
sections.unique_caveat: Molecular-dynamics support is not evidence of biochemical function. The dynamics analysis used MotifBench designs rather than the new BILBY-PRO cases, and the authors describe it as a downstream check, not a sufficient functional test.

sections.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
sections.abstract: In a fixed-budget DiffDock study, geometry-focused or mixed post-training did not consistently outperform broad continuation on returned-pose success.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that broad continuation had the highest mean Top-1 success among the trained policies at the 5 Å threshold, while focused/mixed supervision had no consistent advantage within the tested budget.
sections.unique_caveat: This is one docking architecture and a bounded post-training experiment; RMSD-based pose success does not establish physical validity, interaction recovery or experimental binding.

sections.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
sections.abstract: A primary-care EHR model's colorectal-cancer discrimination improved with longer history up to about 18 years, then plateaued, while an XGBoost baseline reached similar performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose calendar-time lookback as a model-design variable distinct from token context and report that the measured signal plateaued beyond an 18-year lookback in this cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a retrospective prediction study, not a validated screening test. The evaluation is a selected, single-region cohort, discrimination was modest, and the authors note one training run and potential coding/registration biases.

sections.title: Kinetic models of a K channel with 2 stage voltage sensor activation and an opening step
sections.abstract: The paper derives a reduced kinetic description for a potassium channel with two-stage voltage-sensor activation and a separate opening step, relating effective rates to voltage-clamp rate dependence.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author derives conditions under which a 10-state scheme reduces to simpler rate equations with voltage dependence similar to voltage-clamp rates.
sections.unique_caveat: The contribution is kinetic modelling; the abstract does not report new channel experiments or an independent validation dataset.

sections.title: Accelerating reaction network identification via frequency-domain analysis
sections.abstract: The authors use a Fourier-domain approximation to make Bayesian identification of some stochastic intracellular reaction networks less computationally demanding.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that, for certain systems, Fourier transformation makes the measurement likelihood approximately Gaussian, enabling faster Bayesian inference.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence described in the abstract is a numerical observation and one illustrative transcription example; applicability to broader network classes or measured biological datasets remains to be established.

sections.title: High resolution 3D localization of ultrasound sparse sources using a SAGE algorithm
sections.abstract: A SAGE source-localization method achieved 0.24 mm localization-error standard deviation in simulations and improved spatial resolution on experimental proton-induced nanodroplet-vaporization data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report sub-millimeter agreement between vaporization maps and proton distributions in three spatial dimensions, suggesting a possible proton-therapy monitoring application.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes simulations and a specific experimental setup, not a clinical validation cohort or evidence of improved treatment outcomes.

sections.title: Evaluation of Image Noise from Computed Tomography in an Organ-Specific Anthropomorphic Phantom
sections.abstract: In an adult-sized anthropomorphic phantom on one CT scanner, the authors compare organ-specific image noise under ASiR-V and deep-learning reconstruction across noise-index settings and estimate dose reductions at equivalent noise.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a power-law relationship between noise index and CTDIvol and a maximum estimated absolute dose reduction of 1.3 mGy in the liver at one setting.
sections.unique_caveat: Phantom measurements and a modeled dose-equivalence calculation do not establish patient dose reduction, diagnostic non-inferiority or clinical benefit.

sections.title: Continuous Space-Time Finite Element Simulations for Biomedical Flows with Large Boundary Motion and Time-Periodicity
sections.abstract: An axisymmetric space-time finite-element method models periodic flow with moving boundaries and is demonstrated for an intra-aortic balloon pump inside a rigid tube.
sections.claimed_contribution: The method incorporates large boundary motion without remeshing and computes periodic solutions directly; its demonstration resolves jets and recirculation in a rigid-tube model.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a numerical-method demonstration rather than patient-specific or in-vivo evidence; the tube is rigid and does not validate clinical hemodynamic predictions.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: This small batch emphasizes multimodal biology models and evaluation beyond aggregate computational metrics, experimental follow-up in agentic drug discovery, and medical-physics methods whose evidence remains simulation-, phantom-, or setup-specific.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Follow computational protein and docking evaluations with blinded biochemical/structural assays; test genomic, EHR and network-model generalization on independent datasets; and replicate medical-physics methods across acquisition setups and anatomy before making broader translational claims.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The strongest signal is methodological: papers increasingly distinguish computational predictions from physical, experimental, or clinical evidence. PharmAgents2 reports experimental follow-up, while most selected studies remain computational, retrospective, simulated or phantom-based.
